description:
Two timing-sensitive tests fail under parallel build load and pass in isolation, each costing a diagnosis cycle during gate batteries. They encode wall-clock margins that assume an unloaded machine; the fix is to remove the dependence on real time by injecting a mockable clock.

## Background

Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03, session 2):

- `test_worktree_list_excludes_expired_leases` (crates/jit/tests/worktree_cli_tests.rs:436): "both live leases should be counted before expiry: left 1, right 2" — the lease TTL elapsed before the assertion because concurrent worker builds slowed the host. Failed a cargo-ci gate run for issue 3d9e9222.
- `storage::heartbeat::tests::test_background_thread_updates_heartbeat` (crates/jit/src/storage/heartbeat.rs): failed a cargo-ci gate run for story bb7d57a2 under the same conditions.

Both assert against real elapsed time, so a slow host races them to failure.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: lease expiry and heartbeat freshness read the current time from an injectable clock abstraction rather than directly from the system clock, so a test can advance time deterministically.
- [hard] REQ-02: `test_worktree_list_excludes_expired_leases` drives expiry through the injected clock and passes reliably with the full workspace suite running alongside a parallel `cargo build` on the same host.
- [hard] REQ-03: `test_background_thread_updates_heartbeat` verifies heartbeat updates without dependence on real wall-clock margins and passes reliably under the same concurrent-load conditions.
title: Deflake timing-sensitive lease and heartbeat tests
